chapter: Brass bands, Buddy Petit and horns
title: Brass bands and the trombone players he knew
summary: He played in many street brass bands and names trombonists he remembers, such as Ambrose Powers and George Washington.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you ever play much in brass bands on the street? I know I used to hear you a few years ago. Yeah. Oh, Kid Thomas was telling us. He used to play with you. Yeah.
I played in all of them brass bands and played many, many, many, many, many. Three years ago.
Yeah. I played in all the brass land and played many, many, many, many, many, many, many rain down this morning, said nothing. Many pervades, and a rain down.
I ran down all the trombone players, actually, to the stage. I called them all, I called all about four or fifty.
Who are the names of them?

Yeah, they're dead. Just a few around. Yeah, I remember. I mean, what are their names? Oh, some of them I forgot their names. Ambrose. Ambrose Powers. George Washington. I called them Booger Man. I love them. Black, black, black. We used to call them Booger Man. And he was from over there. I asked him to go over there.
